column4: Open the public homepage and click Launch App. The browser should enter the current HTTPS application address and show the role selection dialog. If the environment is unavailable, ask the demonstration operator to check the Mac and tunnels.
column5: Select the intended role before connecting the wallet.

column4: Select the role, choose Rabby and click Connect wallet and sign in. In the extension, check the account, application domain, role and Chain ID before signing. A successful login opens the corresponding workspace without transferring funds.
column5: Continue in the selected role's workspace.

column4: Click Create new series in the top bar. Enter the product name, acknowledge that this is a test and confirm deployment. The new draft has separate contracts and does not appear in the investor hall until fundraising is published.
column5: Ask the owner to select this same product before applying.

column4: Click Receive test funds in the top bar and check the wallet balances. The faucet supplies demo gas and the selected product's test USDC. It does not create an investment or issue DRS, and another product may have a different test USDC contract.
column5: The investor can subscribe after qualification is approved.

column4: Open My stations and select the station details entry. Check the station identity, capacity and evidence timestamp before starting an application. The station list and the single-station dashboard serve different purposes.
column5: Review the detailed evidence and then submit an application.

column4: Review generation, export, devices, alerts and the source badge in Station details. Recorded replay describes an earlier collection and is not a live reading. ALL_OFFLINE is the reported telemetry status and does not by itself invalidate a blockchain product.
column5: Submit the revenue-right application for the selected station.

column4: Select the station and enter the requested information in the application form. Submit the record and retain its application identifier. This step stores the application and evidence references without minting an NFT or issuing investor shares.
column5: The intermediary reviews the application queue.

column4: Open Application review and find the row for the relevant product and station. Check its status and next handler, then open the detailed record. Use the application identifier to distinguish separate requests for the same station.
column5: Review the evidence and terms in the application detail.

column4: Check station identity, evidence, the proposed rights scope and collection responsibilities. Approve complete materials or request supplementation with a clear explanation. A rejected or incomplete application must be resolved before pricing continues.
column5: Prepare the revenue-right offer for an approved application.

column4: Open Quotes and valuation for the approved application. Review historical sample quality, seasonal generation and export estimates, delivered self-use, tariffs, owner discount, costs, FX and discounting. Record the reason for any provisional baseline before generating the offer.
column5: The trustee independently reviews the offer and assumptions.

column4: Open the application in the review queue and compare the forecast with its evidence and assumptions. Explicitly acknowledge provisional data when justified, then approve the offer. Approval does not sign the owner's agreement or transfer funds.
column5: The owner reviews and accepts the approved offer.

column4: Open the approved quote and inspect the monthly timeline from left to right. For each period, compare generation, export, delivered self-use, the grid-price comparison, the owner's discounted payment, export income, costs and discounted present value. These are forecasts rather than recorded receipts.
column5: Accept only after the price and future payment obligation are understood.

column4: Check the rights percentage, five-year term, purchase price, deductions and discounted electricity payment rule. Click Accept for the approved offer. Acceptance records consent to these terms and does not yet mint the station credential.
column5: Sign the corresponding agreement with the owner wallet.

column4: Read the agreement and request the wallet signature. Verify the station, product, Chain ID, price, term and content digest in the message. The signature records agreement acceptance off-chain without transferring equipment ownership.
column5: The intermediary mints the station identity credential.

column4: In Pool management, open the signed application and click Mint station credential. Confirm the transaction with the intermediary wallet. After confirmation, the station NFT belongs to the owner and the transaction can be checked in Blockscout.
column5: The owner authorizes custody by this pool.

column4: Open the agreement's custody task and check the station NFT and destination vault. Authorize this pool in the wallet and wait for chain confirmation. Approval permits custody but is not itself admission into the pool.
column5: The intermediary executes admission after authorization is confirmed.

column4: Check the signed agreement, owner authorization, purchase price and rights term, then execute admission. Confirm that the station NFT is held by the vault and the agreement digest is recorded. Admission does not mint investor shares.
column5: Prepare the pool valuation.

column4: Prepare the pool report after reconciling rights value, cash, receivables, liabilities and future pool expenses. Confirm the submission transaction and retain its report digest and validity period. A material cashflow change may require a new report.
column5: The trustee approves the submitted report.

column4: Review the current report and explicitly check the assumptions acknowledgement before clicking Approve and anchor valuation. Confirm with the trustee wallet. An expired or changed report must return to the intermediary for preparation rather than being forced through approval.
column5: The intermediary publishes fundraising after approval.

column4: Open Product operations and review projected net IRR, expected distributions, reserve policy, target, price and deadline. Publish the issuance terms with the wallet. Investors can then see the product as Fundraising, although no investor shares have been issued yet.
column5: Investors review the published product and apply for qualification.

column4: Open Product hall and select a published Fundraising or Active product. Check its status, cadence, target and contract before entering details. Draft contracts are management work and are excluded from the investor hall.
column5: Review the product timeline and eligibility requirements.

column4: Read the monthly timeline in Pool details. Distinguish the initial investment, monthly collections, accrued expenses, declared distributions, retained cash and remaining NAV. The projected net IRR is a model result and is not the valuation discount rate or a guaranteed coupon.
column5: Apply for qualification before subscribing.

column4: Open Investment qualification, read the risk statement and acknowledge the test-only setting. Submit the application for the connected wallet and selected product. A staff member must approve it before the contract accepts a subscription.
column5: The intermediary reviews this wallet's qualification.

column4: Open the qualification queue, select the investor and review the application. Approve the correct wallet for the selected product and confirm the on-chain transaction. Choosing an investor role in the UI does not grant eligibility.
column5: The investor receives test funds and submits a subscription.

column4: Enter the additional amount in Subscription and check the remaining capacity and wallet balance. Confirm USDC approval if requested, then confirm the subscription transaction. Each addition increases cumulative escrow and invalidates the earlier order review. Repeat subscriptions remain available while fundraising permits them.
column5: The intermediary reviews the latest cumulative amount before settlement.

column4: Open the order and click the refund action before issuance settlement. Confirm the wallet transaction and check that the full cumulative escrow returns to the wallet. This cancels the pending investment without issuing DRS.
column5: The investor may subscribe again while fundraising remains open.

column4: In Product operations, locate the investor's order and compare wallet, cumulative escrow and issuance terms. Approve the latest review version with the intermediary wallet. Approval does not issue shares, and a later addition requires another review.
column5: Settle only when every order and all funding conditions are satisfied.

column4: Check that all orders are approved and the subscription total covers signed purchases plus the 10% initial cash retention. The contract retains the cash automatically during settlement. If a shortfall is shown, direct the investor to add exactly that amount and review the updated order before settling.
column5: The owner receives the purchase payment and investors inspect their issued shares.

column4: Open My holdings after settlement and refresh the confirmed state. Check DRS, the settlement record, the latest approved NAV and any declared distribution. Wallet USDC, subscription escrow and investment NAV are different amounts.
column5: The intermediary begins monthly collection and accounting.

column4: Use Locate operation for the monthly fee task. If its cutoff has not arrived, choose the offered financial-time shortcut and read the shared-clock confirmation. Advancing the test clock affects all products on the chain and does not create live telemetry or approve valuations.
column5: Record completed service periods and reconcile the opening NAV before accruing fees.

column4: Under Monitoring & evidence, check the service period and complete recorded history month. Review the household bill, export income, station costs and FX, then use marker 1 to publish and confirm the wallet transaction.
column5: The invoice binds the designated household, exact test-USDC payment and evidence digest. No cash has been collected yet. The owner pays next.

column2: Approve and pay the monthly bill
column4: Under Funds & monthly bills, check the product, period, token and amount. Use marker 1, approve the exact invoice amount in the wallet and then confirm payment. Explicitly claim test funds first if the balance is insufficient.
column5: The household wallet transfers the bill amount into the billing contract. The invoice awaits intermediary reconciliation. A direct token transfer does not settle a named bill.

column4: Under Monitoring & evidence, inspect the same invoice and household-payment status. Use marker 1 to record only the explicitly simulated grid-export receipt.
column5: A separate system account funds the export component. It does not replace or top up the household payment. Both components await reconciliation.

column2: Reconcile and confirm receipt into the pool
column4: Inspect the household payment, export receipt, station expense and net amount on the same invoice. Use marker 1 to reconcile and confirm receipt into the pool, then confirm the intermediary wallet transaction.
column5: The billing contract pays agreed station expenses once and transfers assigned net proceeds to the vault. The receivable clears once. Completed historical collections are not charged again. Continue with monthly fees and valuation approval.

column4: Check the fee cutoff and the approved opening NAV for this fee period. If the basis is missing, follow the guide to prepare a report and obtain trustee approval. Accrue the monthly annual-fee fraction and mandatory pool costs once. Accrual records liabilities rather than another immediate cash payment.
column5: Prepare the post-accounting valuation for trustee approval.

column4: Prepare a report after receipts and fee accrual are reconciled. The trustee must check the current report and approve its anchor transaction. An older fully paid distribution must not replace this pending approval task. Reprepare a report whose inputs or validity have changed.
column5: Return to the intermediary for the monthly distribution declaration.

column4: After the current report is approved, declare the due monthly distribution. The contract pays applicable accrued expenses, restores six months of mandatory-cost reserve and allocates eligible remaining receipts 75% to distribution and 25% to redemption liquidity. The initial retained cash is not treated as distributable revenue.
column5: Follow the explicit handoff to the investor to inspect and claim this new distribution.

column4: Open My holdings and locate the newly declared distribution identifier. Check the positive claimable amount, confirm Claim in Rabby and compare the wallet balance before and after confirmation. A paid record remains historical and must not continue to appear as payable.
column5: Staff can reconcile the next month after the claim or explicitly defer investor viewing.

column4: After the six-month lock, enter the eligible buyer, share quantity and negotiated USDC total in Transfers and exits. Submit the exact terms and inspect the NAV comparison. A proposal does not itself transfer shares or collect payment.
column5: Investor B accepts these terms and authorizes payment.

column4: Open the proposed transfer and verify the seller, shares and total consideration. Complete the required USDC approval and buyer-consent transactions in the indicated order. Consent is bound to these exact terms and cannot be supplied by the seller.
column5: Obtain intermediary price review if the deviation exceeds 10%.

column4: Open Transfer review and compare the negotiated price with the approved NAV reference. Record the required approval for a deviation above 10%. Review does not guarantee the price or complete either transfer leg.
column5: The seller completes atomic settlement.

column4: Check buyer consent, allowance, eligibility, lock and required review, then confirm settlement. A successful transaction transfers shares to the buyer and USDC to the seller together. Verify both token transfers in Blockscout.
column5: Both investors review their updated positions.

column4: Before the notice cutoff, enter the shares to redeem and confirm the request. The shares enter escrow and remain entitled to distributions until paid. The request is not an immediate cash redemption at today's reference NAV.
column5: The intermediary processes an eligible quarterly dealing window after the lock.

column4: At the eligible dealing date, reconcile and approve the dealing NAV before processing requests. Payment is capped by the lower of redemption liquidity and 5% of pool NAV. The contract pays and burns only filled shares and carries the unfilled balance forward.
column5: The investor checks payment, burned shares and the remaining escrow request.

column4: Before the next cutoff, cancel the outstanding unpaid portion of the redemption request. Confirm that these escrowed shares return to the wallet. Already paid and burned shares cannot be cancelled.
column5: Continue holding or submit a later request if appropriate.

column4: Open Monitoring and evidence and document the reason, supporting evidence and proposed collection-recipient change. Create the case and inspect its fixed ownership snapshot. Ordinary forecast underperformance is not automatically a household default.
column5: Investors review the case and may support it using snapshot weights.

column4: Read the case and the proposed recipient, then confirm support with the investor wallet. The contract uses the fixed snapshot and requires 30% support before trustee action. Later transfers cannot create duplicate voting weight.
column5: Trustee A independently reviews the eligible case.

column4: Open the case, check evidence, snapshot support and recipient, then approve with trustee A's wallet. The contract records this distinct address but does not yet execute the recipient change.
column5: Trustee B performs a separate review of the same case.

column4: Switch to trustee B's configured wallet and sign in again. Review the same case independently and approve it. Two different trustee addresses are required to authorize the demo collection-recipient change, which does not control equipment or a real bank account.
column5: The intermediary checks execution and continues servicing.

column4: After all 60 service months, reconcile receivables, accrued liabilities and distributions, then obtain the final required valuation approval. Confirm Close product when every condition is satisfied. Remaining cash becomes a final distribution rather than an invented repayment of original principal.
column5: Investors claim remaining amounts and the owner retrieves the station credential.

column4: Review every unpaid distribution in My holdings and claim the amounts belonging to this wallet. Check the confirmed USDC transfers. Previously paid distributions are not paid again, and a remaining historical DRS balance does not extend expired revenue rights.
column5: The owner completes station credential release.

column4: Open the expired agreement's release task after product closure. Confirm the release transaction and check that the station NFT returns from the vault to the owner. Equipment ownership remained with the owner throughout the agreement.
column5: The product lifecycle is complete and its transaction history remains queryable.
